title: GitHub CLI logins
whyItMatters: The GitHub CLI keeps an OAuth token for every signed-in GitHub account in this folder. With that token a stranger can act as the person on GitHub, including reading private repositories.
source: GitHub CLI manual, environment: config defaults to ~/.config/gh, or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gh when set - https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_help_environment
notes: hosts.yml holds the per-host user and oauth_token; config.yml in the same folder holds preferences only. GH_CONFIG_DIR can move it. Newer versions may keep the token in the macOS Keychain instead.

cleanup.signOut: Revoke the GitHub CLI authorization in the GitHub account Settings under Applications, so the token stored on this Mac stops working.
steps: Revoke the GitHub CLI token in the GitHub account Settings under Applications.
Delete the file named in the plan using Finder.
Check the account's authorized applications again for anything you do not recognise.
cleanup.risk: Removes the saved GitHub CLI login from this Mac. A token that is not revoked at GitHub keeps working until it expires.
cleanup.source: GitHub CLI manual, gh auth logout: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_auth_logout
